formulas.formula: For sales pros: track deals, quota and commission, and budget around paychecks that change.
1. Setup: your base pay, monthly quota, commission rates (up to and above quota), how many months after a deal closes you get paid, and your tax estimate.
2. Budget: your monthly bills and spending. The goal is to live on your base pay and treat commission as the bonus.
3. Deals: log every deal with its close date and status. For open deals, add your chance of closing.
4. Monthly: sales vs quota, commission earned, commission paid (after the delay), take-home pay and the budget check.
5. Dashboard: this month, the whole year, commission still owed to you, and your top open deals.
Sales up to your quota earn the first rate. Every dollar above quota earns the higher rate.
Many companies pay commission a month after the deal closes. Set 0 if you're paid the same month.
Commission earned but not paid yet, because of the delay. Great for planning big purchases.
Open deals x your chance of closing. Blank chance = 50%. A forecast, not a promise.
If your base take-home covers your budget, every commission check can go to goals and savings.
Clear the white cells on Deals and Budget, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: closed, quota hit, or covered.
Red: lost, short, or something to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Go crush that quota.
The basics. Everything else uses these.
Optional: pick a date to preview that month. Blank = today.
Your salary or draw, before tax.
Blank = no quota (one rate on everything).
Commission paid how many months after closing
Estimate. Commission is often taxed at a higher rate.
Commission still owed from last year

Every deal. For open deals, Close Date is when you expect it to close. Blank chance = 50%.
Commission Earned is what this month's sales earn. Commission Paid is what lands in your paycheck after the delay.
